messages:
cheng: Heads-up — saw steady KV-cache growth and a burst of PT hole warnings when running the longctx PagedAttention repro on H100 with NVLink. Memory doesn't drop after evict, reuse rate tanked.

lisa: Can you paste the logs/snippet? which branch/runtime?

cheng: Running main + small local kvcache tweak. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-19 09:12:03] KVCache: alloc page idx=0x3aF size=64KB owner=worker-7
[2026-03-19 09:12:03] PT: hole detected idx=0x3aF state=STALE_REF cnt=0 refcount=0
[2026-03-19 09:12:03] Evict: scheduled page 0x3aF -> pending fence fd=1024
[2026-03-19 09:12:03] Evict: complete (gpu sync) but PT shows owner!=NULL
[2026-03-19 09:12:05] KVCache: reuse miss spike=+11% longctx=256kb
```
Notably PT shows owner!=NULL after evict, so subsequent allocs rebind stale slot -> fragmentation.

sam: Huh. Sounds like an ordering problem between the device-side writeback and host-side PTA updates. Could be missing a GPU fence or we drain writeback too early on NVLink.

maria: We saw similar non-monotonic allocs on MI250X earlier (different symptom — we got double-free assertions instead). HW memory flush semantics differ; kernel selection for evict path varies (async copy vs direct DMA) which changes timing.

infra-bot: Trace summary for thread 1735551212: p999 latency spike during evict window, pte-writes delayed ~1.8ms on H100 NVLink interconnect. Reproducer job #r-984 ran on 3 hosts.

cheng: Repro command I used: 
```bash
GPUTYPE=h100 ./tools/run_repro --script repro/longctx_pagedattn.py --iters 12000 --batch 16 --kv-window 8192
```
I can attach perf traces (perf.data and nvtx).

lisa: Please attach nvprof / nsight capture. Also try toggling KVCACHE_EVICT_FENCE=1 (env) to force host fence before pt update.

sam: If that helps, we should add an opt-in runtime check: after evict and host fence, assert pt->owner==NULL before reuse. Might bloat perf but good for CI.

cheng: Quick local numbers: without fence env -> mem growth +48MB over 10k iters. With KVCACHE_EVICT_FENCE=1 -> growth ~ +2MB and reuse hit recovers +7%. CPU-side overhead ~0.4%.

maria: On MI250, injecting fence made double-free surface deterministically (kernel race); that HW's evict latency pattern differs. So a single global fence won't be universal fix.

sam: OK — likely two separate issues layered: 1) missing ordering on NVLink path -> stale PT writes; 2) refcount/owner semantics fragile on MI250 when evict uses a different kernel (cuda async vs rocm direct).

lisa: Can we instrument the PT update path to add a sequence number (monotonic) and detect reorder? e.g., pt.seq++ on evict; when allocating, check seq unchanged. Low overhead atomic.

cheng: I prototyped seq check: cuts repro rate by ~90% on H100. Code snippet: 
```c
uint32_t old = atomic_load(&pt->seq);
// after evict completion: atomic_fetch_add(&pt->seq, 1);
// on alloc: if (atomic_load(&pt->seq) != expected) goto retry_alloc;
```
works on H100 but MI250 runs into another path where pt->seq gets incremented twice due to async callback ordering.

sam: Then we should unify the completion callback ordering: ensure device-side completion -> callback serialized onto the same queue that updates PT. Also add a small per-arch shim: for MI250 use callback funnel that dedups increments.

maria: I can share the MI250 timing traces later. Also let's check kernel selection tables: eviction currently picks 'async_copy' for A100/H100 but 'direct_d2h' for MI250; that explains timing delta.

cheng: Actionables: 1) Add seq check in evict path behind env flag (cheng). 2) Add CI job that runs longctx PagedAttention repro on H100 + MI250 (lisa). 3) Add telemetry counter for stale-pt events and reuse-miss spikes (sam). 4) Investigate kernel selection policy to prefer consistent ordering (maria).

lisa: I'm going to spin up MI250 job and test cheng's seq branch, will report back in this thread.

infra-bot: Issue created: KVCACHE-4523 "PT ordering & eviction races across GPU interconnects" assigned to cheng,maria,sam. Link: <internal/issue/KVCACHE-4523>

cheng: Thanks all — attaching nvtx timeline + small perf diff in artifacts; will open PR with seq-check behind flag.

sam: Great. If we can reproduce with deterministic repro and CI gating, we can land detection first then work on removal of flag after fixes. :thumbsup:

lisa: Running MI250 now (job 984-2). Will ping when results in ~45m.

cheng: ping — I added a small debug endpoint: `curl localhost:8080/_debug/kv/stale-pt-count` returns a number. Current dev run shows 17.

maria: FYI — looked at the MI250 trace; kernel selection root cause is in kernel_selector.cpp line ~412 where arch==MI250 picks d2h. I'll prototype a microbenchmark to compare eviction latency variance.

lisa: MI250 run finished: seq-check reduced double-free reproducer but still seeing occasional reuse miss spikes (5% of prior). Uploading logs.

cheng: Good progress. Keep thread updates brief — we'll summarize findings in issue and iterate on a per-arch ordering shim.

maria: I'll draft a design note on "evict completion ordering abstraction" and share tomorrow.

sam: Thanks — setting up a short sync Friday to decide next steps.
